sekcje: Drug Levels and Effects > Summary of Use during Lactation

Rifamycin is negligibly absorbed orally and used only for gastrointestinal infections. It is not likely to reach the breastmilk or bloodstream of the infant or cause any adverse effects in breastfed infants after maternal use. If a mother requires rifamycin, it is not a reason to discontinue breastfeeding.
